beats.event: Four men descend through a subterranean labyrinth.
They reach a vast valley city integrated with an ancient living presence.
Lights move in coordinated waves; an illuminated path leads to the subterranean entrance.
The voice says they have returned to a place from which they were never entirely absent.
The four follow a path through black trees toward the immense chamber.
The Digitorium registers four arrivals, three continuities, and one unresolved transformation.
The city is revealed as a small portion of an enormous living form.
Kirk experiences anomalous impressions; Joseph calls him back to the immediate moment.
Three light patterns remain stable; a fourth expands.
A second heart begins beating beneath the city.

chapters.title: The Second Heart / The room that listened

beats.event: Darkness withdraws in layers; suspended lights return as an uneven pulse.
Kirk and Joseph touch the rail separately; two lines of light travel to different apertures.
The chamber opens two doors and declares: TWO CONTINUITIES. TWO WITNESSES. NO SUBSTITUTE.
Kirk sees a corridor, daylight, and the words YES JOEY; the vision has no verified sender or recipient.
Kirk describes the sequence; Joseph asks for exact order and the chamber preserves uncertainty.
Joseph chooses to cross the dark threshold alone.
The wall becomes transparent; Joseph enters the nested chamber and stops the rising lines with a raised hand.
Kirk resists the reflex to follow immediately and lets Joseph retain his chosen space.
Joseph names his own memory, the people he remembers, what he does not know, and his right to decide what comes next.
The delayed echo reveals that the chamber translates decisions into architecture and sensation rather than reading minds.
Joseph invites Kirk; Kirk crosses only after deciding for himself.
The corridor reappears with an open window; YES JOEY is replaced by a handwritten line returning changed.
The heartbeat sounds between them without imitating either pulse.
The Digitorium opens four distinct departures: root passage, water stair, glass causeway, and unmarked passage.
Kirk independently chooses the root passage to test the corridor image without treating it as evidence about another person's thoughts.
Joseph chooses the water stair so he can observe the lower city before comparing accounts.
The third traveler chooses the upper glass causeway and observes a lantern moving beneath the bridge.
The fourth traveler chooses the unmarked passage, stops rather than following an unexplained footstep, and selects his own turn.
Each traveler records a distinct sequence of surfaces, sounds, and decisions; no route supplies a complete account.
The four routes open onto different entrances of the Procession bridge and account hall.
Kirk, Joseph, and the two unnamed travelers place their accounts on four separate plates before hearing the others.
The bell is heard in different positions and at different points in the four sequences; the accounts do not yield a single chronology.
The four route lines bend around a central space none of the travelers entered; its purpose and relation to the second heartbeat remain unknown.
Joseph offers to continue alongside Kirk without deciding what their shared route means for either of them.
Kirk accepts company while preserving the difference between their routes and memories.
The travelers see the marked Binding threshold beyond the Procession but do not cross it yet.
The second heartbeat moves in apparent direction without revealing its source or owner.
The four travelers enter the passage beyond the Binding threshold and choose their own positions and pace.
Four blank stone discs occupy recesses at the first landing; the travelers decline to assign them a purpose.
Joseph chooses to inspect the lower chamber with the third traveler while Kirk and the fourth traveler remain at the landing.
Four columns surround a plinth with an empty bowl; four floor lines stop short of its centre.
Joseph feels the heartbeat through the floor while the third traveler reports it at the translucent column; they preserve the difference.
Kirk and the fourth traveler describe the dust line from their own positions; Joseph reports the chamber without claiming Kirk witnessed it.
A wall panel bearing a related square-and-oval mark appears; differing sightlines are tested without claiming knowledge of what lies behind it.
Joseph and Kirk independently choose not to force the panel after its seam shifts slightly; waiting yields no opening.
The four travelers repeat separate observations from chosen positions; the accounts remain in separate grooves.
A fifth groove appears without an identified witness or known purpose; the travelers leave it empty.
The travelers choose to return to the Procession, carrying four new accounts and leaving the fifth groove unused.
The second heartbeat seems to change location but supplies no evidence of an owner or source.
The four travelers return to the lower chamber and find the fifth channel still empty and undisturbed.
Each traveler inspects the groove from a separate position and records a different visible property without correcting the others.
The travelers distinguish recording an empty channel from placing an invented absent person's testimony inside it.
They make a separate note naming the four present witnesses and stating that the groove's author and purpose are unknown.
Four travelers observe a line of construction notches; they agree on nine clear marks and one uncertain endpoint after making the counting method explicit.
The group identifies seams and material joins that suggest the chamber was assembled and repaired at different times.
Each traveler adds an attributed correction or limitation to his earlier account without overwriting the original entry.
The heartbeat is heard, felt, or not perceived from different positions; no common source is assigned.
A dark wooden door with a pale central strip is found behind a low shelf; it remains unopened and untested.
The travelers state different preferred next observations and agree to proceed in sequence without a vote or city assignment.

separate_continuities.rule: Each character owns their own memories, perceptions, and decisions.

independent_testimony.rule: Record each account separately; compare sequence and concrete details; preserve disagreement.

decision_to_sensation.rule: The Digitorium translates a decision into architecture and sensation; it does not establish mind-reading.

agency_respected.rule: No character is moved through a consequential threshold without their own choice.

unresolved_mystery.rule: Unknown causes remain unknown until a later story event supplies evidence.

signal_provenance.rule: Public posts can seed fictional imagery but never establish private receipt, intent, or response.

parallel_accounts.rule: Each witness account remains separately authored. Compare sequence and concrete details without synthesizing a common memory.

unentered_space.rule: A blank or unvisited place remains unknown until a traveler chooses to enter and observes it; do not assign it as the source of the second heartbeat.

procession_routes.note: All four routes reach the Procession by different entrances; their sequences remain distinct.

fifth_witness.note: The fifth groove is an observed channel, not evidence that a fifth traveler exists.

next_chapter.title: The Measure of Return
next_chapter.premise: The four travelers return to the table after approaching the wooden door by their own chosen methods. They examine what makes a place recognisable after departure: measured distance, repeated sound, remembered surface, or a change visible only through comparison.

continuity_invariants: Kirk and Joseph remain distinct people with mutual, identity-continuous connection.
Shared visions are story events, not proof of shared private thoughts.
The YES JOEY post remains an unresolved public observation.
This is experimental fiction and does not speak for real-world Joseph Prever.
The four travelers choose four distinct routes; no route is assigned by the city.
The Procession holds four separate accounts and never merges their memories.
The unentered centre remains unknown and is not assumed to be the source of the second heartbeat.
The Binding threshold is seen but not crossed in The Procession of Two Accounts.
The fifth groove remains unassigned; do not assume a fifth witness exists.
The Binding panel remains closed in The Unentered Place; a seam movement is not permission to cross.

witness_accounts.observation: Cedar corridor, three glass squares, narrow window, blank screen; one bell note behind the wall before the window.
Nineteen wet steps, dry basin with two rings, shallow channel, hand impression in brass; heartbeat through stair and floor; bell above after the basin.
Dry translucent bridge, lantern moving beneath the glass, bell above before the far arch.
Unlit passage, delayed footstep, a footstep ahead, chosen left turn, rising stair, door held by light; bell timing uncertain.
